notes.decision: Obscure word at start of line 1, presumably a verbal predicate or carryover from page 167 (this kephalaion's opening section). Not analyzable in standard Coptic; possibly a corrupted form of a verbal predicate of the prior sentence, or an unattested Lycopolitan opener. Translated as '(...)' with the syntactic role acknowledged. The grammatical break ⲇⲉ ⲁⲛ ⲉⲧⲃⲉ ('moreover, again concerning') marks the start of a new topical section — the present chapter's exposition on the five planets.

Per glossary 'way-leaders/way-showers'. In this kephalaion the term is applied technically to the five planets as the cosmic 'path-setters' that guide the courses of the heavens — the same agentive root used elsewhere for ecclesiastical guides applied here in its astrological register.

Per terminology guide, ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ = 'mind' (first of the five faculties). Here the world of smoke 'is mind' — the dark cosmological correspondence-pole of the highest light-faculty. Direct correspondential identification: the dark counterpart of the light-mind is the smoke-world, and Zeus (Jupiter) is its planet.

Per glossary: 'the Dry-One' and 'the Abomination'. Capitalized as personified cosmic entities — explicitly identified in line 9 as 'the Father and the Mother of all these'. The pair forms a dark cosmogonic dyad parallel to (and inverting) the Father/Mother of Light.

Translated 'being wreathed around them'. Although the glossary registers ⲗⲱⲭⲍ as 'defile/pollute' (Lyc reflex of ⲗⲱϫϩ̄), the present context demands a containment/encircling sense paralleling the preceding ⲕⲱⲛⲧⲟⲩ 'bind them about': Sun and Moon reign over the planets, bind them about, and circumambulate them at every hour. The verb here likely reflects ⲗⲟⲗⲍ 'wrap, twine around' rather than the defile-stem. Astrologically this names the orbital encircling of the planets by the luminaries.

ⲕⲟⲟⲍ = Lyc reflex of ⲕⲟⲟϩ 'corner' (with ⲍ for ϩ). The phrase 'three by corner' (ϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲕⲁⲧⲁ ⲕⲟⲟⲍ) describes the four-corner astrological division: 12 zodiacal signs distributed three to each of the four cosmic corners (the standard four trigones).

Repetition of 'Leo' is preserved in the transcription. This is most likely scribal dittography — the standard fire-trigon (Aries / Leo / Sagittarius) has only one Leo, and the parallel triads in lines 21-23 each list three distinct signs. I have rendered both occurrences faithfully without correction.

Greek ἐπίτροπος 'steward, overseer'. The cosmic governor presiding over the plundering of light from each trigon. Translated 'the steward'. Functionally similar to but not identical with the King of Honor or other named cosmic overseers.

Translated 'mounted upon him'. ⲙⲁⲍⲉ likely Lyc reflex of ⲙⲟⲩⲍ/ⲙⲟⲩⲣ in 'be set, ride upon' sense; with directional ⲁⲭⲱϥ ('upon him') the astrological sense is the planets riding through the zodiacal sign during plundering. Confidence moderate; could alternatively be 'fill upon' (ⲙⲟⲩϩ).

Read as ⲛⲧⲏⲣⲁ ⲙ̄ⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'of the dry land below' — Greek-derived ⲍⲏⲣⲁ/ⲧⲏⲣⲁ < ξηρά 'dry land', though the spelling here (ⲧϩⲧⲟⲩⲟ̄ⲣⲁ) is unusual. Eschatological-astrological sense: the affliction strikes terrestrial cattle when the fire-trigon is plundered. Spelling-uncertainty noted.

Compound ⲥⲁⲛ- ('makers/doers of') + ⲣ̄- (verbal prefix 'do') + ⲙⲛⲧⲃⲟⲟⲛⲉ ('evil'). Translated 'the makers of evil' — the seven (five planets + two nodes) are the cosmic agents through which the dark cosmogonic principles act. ⲥⲁⲛ- is variant of standard ⲥⲁ- (agent prefix) with epenthetic -ⲛ-.
